problem: Wrong magnitude and unit by a factor of 1000. kG = kc/RT with kc = 0.02 m/s and RT = 0.0246 m³·atm/mol gives (m/s)/(m³·atm/mol) = mol/(m²·s·atm), so kG = 0.81 mol/(m²·s·atm), not 0.81 kmol/(m²·s·atm). The stated unit reasoning is also garbled: "mol/m³ divided by m³·atm/mol is mol/(m³·atm)" is not a valid unit operation, and no kmol appears anywhere in the data.
fix: kG = kc/RT = 0.02 (m/s) ÷ 0.0246 (m³·atm/mol) = 0.81 mol/(m²·s·atm) = 8.1 × 10⁻⁴ kmol/(m²·s·atm). Unit check: (m/s) ÷ (m³·atm/mol) = mol/(m²·s·atm). To get kmol/(m²·s·atm) directly, use R = 0.08206 m³·atm/(kmol·K), so RT = 24.6 m³·atm/kmol and kG = 0.02/24.6 = 8.1 × 10⁻⁴ kmol/(m²·s·atm).

where: Section 1, sentence after the formula ("It is the volume of fluid cleared...")
problem: The two 'per' clauses read as m/s per (mol/m³), which is not the unit of kc and can confuse a student. kc already is the flux divided by the concentration difference; it equals a volume per unit area per second only when the concentration difference is unity.
fix: It is the molar flux per unit concentration difference. Numerically, when the concentration difference is 1 mol/m³, it equals the volume of fluid cleared of species A per unit interfacial area per second. It is a transport coefficient, not the speed of the fluid.

where: Section 3, the four-item list (By position / By phase / By combination / By driving force)
problem: The list starts with no lead-in sentence, so it hangs unexplained, and the 'By phase' and 'By driving force' lines partly repeat each other (kc and kL both sit on concentration).
fix: Add a lead such as 'Coefficients are classified in four ways:' and merge the last two lines, e.g. 'By driving force (and so by phase): kc or kL on a concentration difference (m/s), kG on a partial pressure difference (kmol/(m²·s·atm)), ky on a mole fraction difference (kmol/(m²·s)).'
